account:
Today I have repeatedly heard an oddly vague claim about a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Several townsfolk have repeated it, and the neighbour asked the secretary about it, but nobody has supplied a specific event or firsthand evidence. The secretary explicitly says she has seen no change herself. I cannot yet tell whether this is ordinary garbled gossip or something people are arranging without my knowledge, and I do not know its purpose.

I attended the morning mill inspection and observed two stacks of sixty-four hay bales, taking nothing. That count alone gives me no reason to suspect wrongdoing. I looked for the baker at the bakery but did not see him inside. I later saw him at the market stall, and the secretary has just confirmed seeing him waiting there. He is a sensible person to ask directly about the bakery claim.

The builder's delivered bridge report says the crossing and approaches were passable on foot and lit, but explicitly does not certify structural safety or concealed supports. It identifies no specific justified repair, and says no repairs or municipal purchases were made. Its agreed two-emerald fee was due before noon today. I have asked the secretary whether it has been paid, but her latest reply addressed the baker and appointments instead, so payment remains unconfirmed to me.

My confirmed remaining commitments are lunch at home at noon, council letters in the office at one, tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage at three, office at half past four, and home at seven. It is now just after noon and I am still at the town hall. I want to keep those commitments while obtaining concrete accounts rather than treating the repeated rumour as fact.
